current_reality.title: A burden left to the individual
current_reality.summary: The talk questions a private-machine account of the body: relationships and surroundings shape regulation, while responsibility is left with the individual. This is a source argument, not a diagnosis of a named group.

current_reality.title: When a successful intervention harms its surroundings
current_reality.summary: A target can be met while the wider living system responds in unintended ways. The causal connection is an AI inference from the talk’s account of lineal control.

current_reality.title: Whose purposes shape our attention?
current_reality.summary: Anticipatory environments can support people or narrow their agency. The script separates the cited smart-home proposal from Heath’s extension to phones and feeds.

future_reality.title: Offer a practice that people can leave
future_reality.summary: Shared rhythms and consent arrangements act together in the proposed benefit. Pressure and feeling less safe remain possible harms; an opt-out is not proof that pressure has been prevented.

future_reality.title: Let responses change the next move
future_reality.summary: Listening and retuning may support learning. What counts as useful feedback and whether the response changes anything need testing in a bounded setting.

future_reality.title: Ask whether a tool widens choices
future_reality.summary: Assessment is meant to support chosen purposes, but naming a purpose does not itself change a tool’s design or ownership. The connection remains a hypothesis.

overview.title: Shared support with room to choose
overview.text: The proposed goal depends on voluntary participation, the ability to notice strain and repair, and tools whose purposes people can question. These conditions are an AI interpretation of the talk, awaiting review.
link: Inspect the goal and its conditions →

overview.title: The body as a private machine
overview.text: The talks ask what is lost when the body is treated as something to optimise alone. Two other proposed chains concern fixed targets with unintended harms, and technologies whose purposes users did not choose.

overview.title: Arrive together, without owing the room your calm
overview.text: The script offers a short, optional settling practice. This map puts the invitation beside its conditions and risk: some may feel more able to be with others, while some may feel pressure or less safe. No practice has been tried or evaluated here.
link: Inspect the joint condition, possible benefit and harm →

overview.title: Listen, retune, and question the tools
overview.text: The wider proposal is a way of attending: act, notice how bodies, people and environments respond, and change the next move. Ask whether the tools shaping the setting widen people’s choices and whose purposes they serve.
link: Explore the proposed changes and their effects →

overview.title: Body, tools and a wider world
overview.text: The talk travels through embodied cognition, predictive processing and extended minds toward a somatic commons. It distinguishes evidence for coupling, contested extension and a philosophical commitment to participation. This practical reconstruction does not require agreement that tools constitute minds. A willing group, any conflict, prerequisites, assigned actions and participant assessment still need to be established.

overview.title: Whose ideas these are
overview.text: The three supplied PDFs are by Margeret Heath. The AI selected, paraphrased and connected the material, and is responsible for this map. Every item has a page reference and a labelled basis; source credit is not author endorsement.

backlog.label: Identify actual participants and how they would judge benefit and harm.
backlog.note: No willing group, trial owner or feedback commitment is established. Agree a bounded setting, observation opportunity and who would judge benefit and harm before treating a trial as ready.

backlog.label: Check whether declining and raising harm are possible in practice.
backlog.note: Quietness or compliance is not evidence of safety. Ask participants about pressure and whether opting out changes how they are treated.

backlog.label: Check whether consent arrangements actually prevent pressure.
backlog.note: The proposed prevention connection is a hypothesis, not a guarantee. Permission to step out may fail under social pressure.

backlog.label: Check whether assessing a tool changes choices and control.
backlog.note: Naming whose purposes a tool serves does not itself change its design or ownership. Test the link rather than assuming an assessment produces agency.

backlog.label: Establish conflicts, prerequisites and actions with a willing group.
backlog.note: The talk offers invitations and questions, not an agreed five-part conflict, dependency plan or assigned action sequence. Those views are deliberately empty.
